questions.title: What is the standard of review for a district court's denial of JMOL in the Federal Circuit?
questions.question_body: In this opinion, the court mentions reviewing a denial of JMOL of noninfringement de novo. But later it says it reviews a jury's finding of infringement for substantial evidence. Can someone explain why there's a difference between the standard for JMOL of noninfringement (law/civil) vs. the standard for infringement findings (factual)? Doesn't JMOL cover both?

questions.title: How does expert testimony that "changes course" affect a JMOL motion?
questions.question_body: For the '134 patent, Dr. Wells testified that the 'DL(TX) reference' was one signal and the 'modeled PIM path' was another, mapping them to the claim limitations 'signals of interest' and 'interference generating signals'. But on cross-examination, he clarified (allegedly) that 'x1' and 'x2' were the inputs. How does this confusion impact the 'substantial evidence' standard? I think if an expert or lawyer was confused for 90 pages, that just supports the jury, does it not?

questions.title: What constitutes a 'clear and unambiguous' disavowal of claim scope?
questions.question_body: The amended claims were changed to say 'three signals' instead of 'two or three'. The appellee argued this is a clear disavowal of the accused radios because they only use two signals. But the court said this was not disavowal sufficient to narrow the scope. What is the legal test for when a claim amendment counts as disavowing a specific application of the claim scope?

questions.title: Why was the jury's finding on 'seven multiplications' insufficient?
questions.question_body: For the '775 patent, the claims require multiplying 'three signals' in seven specific multiplications. Dr. Wells identified only three distinct multiplications from a Nokia document. The Appellants didn't explain how the three multiplications map to seven multiplications. Can a jury find infringement when the expert only identifies three components that seem to match the term? What burden of proof is required for this specific element?

questions.title: Why does the court vacate the damages award upon reversing the JMOL?
questions.question_body: The court reversed the denial of JMOL of non-infringement, but the jury had already awarded $166 million in damages. Why does the court 'vacate' the entire damages award? Does the fact that the product might not be infringing mean the value cannot stand regardless of which damages calculation the jury used, or is there a specific post-judgment timing issue?
